lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Approximately 92.3% of our total resident revenues from communities that we operated were attributable to private pay sources and approximately 7.7% of our resident revenues from these communities were attributable to reimbursements from Medicaid, in each case, during fiscal year 2025.
For the year ended December 31, 2025, Medicaid reimbursements represented approximately 7.7% of our resident revenues from communities that we operated.

We have a high concentration of communities in various geographic areas, including the states of Texas, Indiana, Ohio and Florida, which we estimate represented approximately 22%, 13%, 18%, and 10%, respectively, of our resident revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025.
Revenues from the Medicaid program accounted for approximately 7.7 % and 10.1 % of the Company’s revenue in fiscal years 2025 and 2024, respectively.

We have a concentration of owned properties operating in Texas ( 20 ), Indiana ( 12 ), Ohio ( 12 ) and Florida ( 8 ), which represented approximately 22 %, 13 %, 18 %, and 10 %, respectively, of our resident revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025 and approximately 23 %, 17 %, 19 %, and 5 %, respectively, of our resident revenues for the year ended December 31, 2024.
• We largely rely on private pay residents and circumstances that adversely affect the ability of the seniors to pay for our services could have a material adverse effect on us.

• We rely on information technology in our operations, and failure to maintain the security and functionality of our information technology and computer systems, or to prevent a cybersecurity attack, breach or other unauthorized access, could adversely affect our business, reputation and relationships with our residents, employees and referral sources and may subject us to remediation costs, government inquiries and liabilities under HIPAA and data and consumer protection laws, any of which could materially and adversely impact our revenues, results of operations, cash flow, and liquidity.
• We rely on the services of key executive officers and the transition of management or loss of these officers or their services could have a material adverse effect on us.

Although we will have some general oversight approval rights and the right to review operational and financial reporting information, our third-party managers are ultimately in control of the day-to-day business of our managed communities, and we will rely on them to operate and manage the communities, including providing resident care, complying with laws, managing risk, setting appropriate resident fees and providing accurate and timely community-level financial results.
In addition, the success of our managed communities, will depend on our ability to maintain good relationships with our third-party managers.

Additionally, because each lease is a triple-net lease, we will depend on our tenants to pay certain insurance, taxes, utilities and maintenance and repair expenses and to indemnify, defend and hold us harmless from and against various claims, litigation and liabilities arising in connection with their business.
We rely on reimbursement from government programs for a portion of our revenues.

We rely upon the proper function and availability of our information technology and computer systems, including hardware, software, applications and electronic data storage, to communicate with our residents and patients, their doctors and other healthcare providers, and our employees and vendors and to store, process, safeguard and transmit our business information, including proprietary business information, private health information and personally identifiable information of our residents and employees.
In addition, we rely on software support of third parties to secure and maintain our information systems and data.

We rely upon the quality of our staff as a means to differentiate our services from other providers.
To cover existing open positions, during 2024 and continuing into 2025, we needed to rely on more expensive premium labor, primarily contract labor and overtime.
We depend on the services of our executive officers for our management.
We are a holding company with no operations and rely on our operating subsidiaries to provide us with funds necessary to meet our financial obligations.
Our decision to issue equity securities in a future offering will depend on market conditions and other factors, some of which are beyond our control.
A public trading market having the desired depth, liquidity and orderliness depends on the presence of a sufficient number of willing buyers and sellers for our common stock at any given time.
We also seek contractual commitments from key suppliers to appropriately secure and maintain their information technology systems and protect our information that is processed on their systems.

The Company’s actual liquidity and capital funding requirements depend on numerous factors, including its operating results, its capital expenditures for community investment, and general economic conditions, as well as other factors described in “Item 1A.
